correctness.rationale: The standard closed-neighborhood initialization fills every occupied clique. An endpoint filled clique sweeps its unique outward matching neighbor in each column; two consecutive filled cliques sweep both outward directions. In the absence of both patterns, every occupied layer is interior and isolated. For at most n-2 seeds, at least two column indices are seed-free. A permanent invariant keeps all those columns unobserved in every unoccupied layer: observed vertices in unoccupied layers retain at least two white neighbors inside their clique; occupied-layer vertices in seed-free columns have two white vertical neighbors; other forces preserve the invariant. Thus propagation fails. n-1 seeds in layer 2 except one column force their missing endpoint clique cell, completing layer 1, and then sweep the remainder, showing sharpness. An independent-set polynomial of the interior layer path counts precisely all failing configurations of degree ≤n-2; coefficient extraction and the Bernoulli support calculation give the formulas. A binomial tail bounds the omitted high-cardinality sets and vanishes under p=c/n with fixed L. The standalone checker exhaustively compared 257426 low-budget subsets, all coefficients, and boundary witnesses across n=3..6 and L=3..7. No appeal to finite tests for the universal theorem is made.

originality.rationale: The substantive claim is a sharp, all-subset criterion through cardinality n-2 for the Cartesian clique path, with an explicitly counted independent-layer obstruction, a sharp n-1 cutoff witness, and a fixed-layer Bernoulli c/n limit. The full text of arXiv:1805.10984v1 supplies the power domination polynomial framework but gives no Cartesian K_n-by-path enumeration. The full text of arXiv:2209.03930v1 supplies bounds for Cartesian products but not this set classification. The accessible sections of Koh--Soh supply the minimum-value observation for the same graph, which is expressly not claimed as new. Published record summaries about power domination of book graphs, spider trees, connected threshold graphs and chain graphs concern different objects and do not imply this criterion. Equivalent graph notations and fort-based dual conditions were considered; none of these specific inspected statements implies the new counting/reliability theorem. Residual priority uncertainty is acknowledged.
residual_risks: The priority search is not exhaustive, and an unindexed equivalent fort-neighborhood or clique-strip formulation might exist.
The accessible 2016 online text has display-math gaps, but its inspected observation establishes only scalar minimum placement; unexpected stronger content could alter priority assessment.
Only finite dimensions were exhaustively tested; the theorem depends on the separately written invariant proof for arbitrary n and L.

value.rationale: The gap is the all-budget sensor placement distribution for a natural Cartesian clique-strip family, not a routine scalar power-domination number. It determines exactly which low-cost multisensor placements observe the entire strip, identifies a sharp failure of the support-only description at n-1 seeds, supplies exact layer-resolved enumerators through a growing degree window and yields a meaningful sparse random-placement observability limit in terms of an independent-set polynomial. The threshold and limiting law cannot be read from the already-known singleton optimum and can be used to distinguish deployment strategies with different sensor counts or layer allocations.
